Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * |date=2009-12-31 |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} }} [[File:SendaiTanabata1.jpg|thumb|220px|right|Example of decorations (August 7, 2005)]] [[File:Tanabata Ornament.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations at a bus stop (August 4, 2007)]] [[File:Sendai tanabata matsuri 2008-8-8.webm|right|thumb|220px|Sendai Tanabata Matsuri (August 8, 2008)]] [[File:Vegalta SENDAI Tanabata, the decorations of Sendai Star Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting {{ill|Vegalta Sendai|ja|ベガルタ仙台}} (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} * The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Jap[[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]]an utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. [[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 2]] == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭}} *
