is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭|1=Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/festival|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuri|qq=}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Domain|qq=}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanabata|qq=}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai|qq=}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 7|qq=}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 7|qq=}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/arcade|qq=}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Station|qq=}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Masamune|qq=}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmei Famine|qq=}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦|1=Solar calendar|2=ja|3=太陽暦|4=de|5=Solarkalender|6=fr|7=Calendrier solaire|8=it|9=Calendario solare|10=ru|11=Солнечный календарь|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/solar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Solar calendar|qq=}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 6|qq=}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8|qq=}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Air Raid|qq=}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōwa Emperor|qq=}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese economic miracle|qq=}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Orizuru|qq=}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinchaku|qq=}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōami|qq=}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Orihime|qq=}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kusudama|qq=}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭|1=Japanese festivals|lt=Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/festival|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuri|qq=}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Domain|qq=}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanabata|qq=}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai|qq=}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 7|qq=}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 7|qq=}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/arcade|qq=}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Station|qq=}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Masamune|qq=}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmei Famine|qq=}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦|1=Solar calendar|2=ja|3=太陽暦|4=de|5=Solarkalender|6=fr|7=Calendrier solaire|8=it|9=Calendario solare|10=ru|11=Солнечный календарь|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/solar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Solar calendar|qq=}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 6|qq=}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8|qq=}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Air Raid|qq=}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōwa Emperor|qq=}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese economic miracle|qq=}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Orizuru|qq=}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinchaku|qq=}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōami|qq=}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Orihime|qq=}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kusudama|qq=}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks festivals|lt=Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/festival|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuri|qq=}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Domain|qq=}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanabata|qq=}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai|qq=}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 7|qq=}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 7|qq=}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/arcade|qq=}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Station|qq=}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Masamune|qq=}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmei Famine|qq=}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦|1=Solar calendar|2=ja|3=太陽暦|4=de|5=Solarkalender|6=fr|7=Calendrier solaire|8=it|9=Calendario solare|10=ru|11=Солнечный календарь|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/solar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Solar calendar|qq=}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 6|qq=}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8|qq=}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Air Raid|qq=}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōwa Emperor|qq=}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese economic miracle|qq=}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Orizuru|qq=}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinchaku|qq=}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōami|qq=}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Orihime|qq=}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kusudama|qq=}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai|qq=}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 7|qq=}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 7|qq=}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/arcade|qq=}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Station|qq=}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Masamune|qq=}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmei Famine|qq=}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and {{ill|festival|ja|祭|1=Japanese festivals|lt=Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/festival|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsuri|qq=}} held throughout the former {{ill|Sendai Domain|ja|仙台藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Domain|qq=}} to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=}}, {{ill|Tanabata|ja|七夕|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanabata|qq=}}. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in {{ill|Sendai|ja|仙台市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai|qq=}}, is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with {{ill|August 7|ja|8月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 7|qq=}}, the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 7|qq=}} in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other {{ill|arcade|ja|アーケード (建築物)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/arcade|qq=}} streets around {{ill|Sendai Station|ja|仙台駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Station|qq=}}. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by {{ill|Date Masamune|ja|伊達政宗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Date Masamune|qq=}}, the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the {{ill|Tenmei Famine|ja|天明の大飢饉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmei Famine|qq=}}, a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the {{ill|solar calendar|ja|太陽暦|1=Solar calendar|2=ja|3=太陽暦|4=de|5=Solarkalender|6=fr|7=Calendrier solaire|8=it|9=Calendario solare|10=ru|11=Солнечный календарь|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/solar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Solar calendar|qq=}}, further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to {{ill|August 6|ja|8月6日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/August 6|qq=}}–{{ill|8|ja|8月8日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/8|qq=}}, aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the {{ill|Sendai Air Raid|ja|仙台空襲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Air Raid|qq=}}. It was fully restored in 1947 during the {{ill|Shōwa Emperor|ja|昭和天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōwa Emperor|qq=}}’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during {{ill|Japanese economic miracle|ja|高度経済成長|lt=Japan's postwar economic growth|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese economic miracle|qq=}}, evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * {{ill|Orizuru|ja|折鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Orizuru|qq=}}: Longevity. * {{ill|Kinchaku|ja|巾着|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinchaku|qq=}}: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * {{ill|Tōami|ja|投網|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōami|qq=}}: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=}}: Threads woven by {{ill|Orihime|ja|織姫|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Orihime|qq=}}. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=}}, often paired with {{ill|kusudama|ja|くす玉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kusudama|qq=}}. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks supporting [[:en:Vegalta Sendai|Vegalta Sendai]] (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and [[:en:Festival|Matsuri]] held throughout the former [[:en:Sendai Domain|Sendai Domain]] to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=}}, [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]]. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with [[:en:August 7|August 7]], the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of [[:en:July 7|July 7]] in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other [[:en:Arcade (architecture)|arcade]] streets around [[:en:Sendai Station (Miyagi)|Sendai Station]]. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by [[:en:Date Masamune|Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the [[:en:Great Tenmei famine|Tenmei Famine]], a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the [[:en:Solar calendar|Solar calendar]], further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to [[:en:August 6|August 6]]–[[:en:August 8|8]], aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the [[:en:Bombing of Sendai in World War II|Sendai Air Raid]]. It was fully restored in 1947 during the [[:en:Hirohito|Shōwa Emperor]]’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during [[:en:Japanese economic miracle|Japan's postwar economic growth]], evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * [[:en:Orizuru|Orizuru]]: Longevity. * [[:en:Kinchaku|Kinchaku]]: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * [[:en:Cast net|Tōami]]: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=}}: Threads woven by [[:en:Zhinü|Orihime]]. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=}}, often paired with [[:en:Kusudama|kusudama]]. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other [[:en:Arcade (architecture)|arcade]] streets around [[:en:Sendai Station (Miyagi)|Sendai Station]]. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by [[:en:Date Masamune|Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the [[:en:Great Tenmei famine|Tenmei Famine]], a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the [[:en:Solar calendar|Solar calendar]], further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to [[:en:August 6|August 6]]–[[:en:August 8|8]], aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the [[:en:Bombing of Sendai in World War II|Sendai Air Raid]]. It was fully restored in 1947 during the [[:en:Hirohito|Shōwa Emperor]]’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during [[:en:Japanese economic miracle|Japan's postwar economic growth]], evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * [[:en:Orizuru|Orizuru]]: Longevity. * [[:en:Kinchaku|Kinchaku]]: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * [[:en:Cast net|Tōami]]: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=}}: Threads woven by [[:en:Zhinü|Orihime]]. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=}}, often paired with [[:en:Kusudama|kusudama]]. [[File:SendaiTanabata1.jpg|thumb|220px|right|Example of decorations (August 7, 2005)]] [[File:Tanabata Ornament.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations at a bus stop (August 4, 2007)]] [[File:Sendai tanabata matsuri 2008-8-8.webm|right|thumb|220px|Sendai Tanabata Matsuri (August 8, 2008)]] [[File:Vegalta SENDAI Tanabata, the decorations of Sendai Star Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting [[:en:Vegalta Sendai|Vegalta Sendai]] (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and [[:en:Festival|Matsuri]] held throughout the former [[:en:Sendai Domain|Sendai Domain]] to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=}}, [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]]. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with [[:en:August 7|August 7]], the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of [[:en:July 7|July 7]] in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other [[:en:Arcade (architecture)|arcade]] streets around [[:en:Sendai Station (Miyagi)|Sendai Station]]. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by [[:en:Date Masamune|Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the [[:en:Great Tenmei famine|Tenmei Famine]], a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the [[:en:Solar calendar|Solar calendar]], further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to [[:en:August 6|August 6]]–[[:en:August 8|8]], aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the [[:en:Bombing of Sendai in World War II|Sendai Air Raid]]. It was fully restored in 1947 during the [[:en:Hirohito|Shōwa Emperor]]’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during [[:en:Japanese economic miracle|Japan's postwar economic growth]], evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * [[:en:Orizuru|Orizuru]]: Longevity. * [[:en:Kinchaku|Kinchaku]]: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * [[:en:Cast net|Tōami]]: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=}}: Threads woven by [[:en:Zhinü|Orihime]]. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=}}, often paired with [[:en:Kusudama|kusudama]]. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|qq=}} * {{ill|Zuihōden Tanabata supporting [[:en:Vegalta Sendai|Vegalta Sendai]] (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and [[:en:Festival|Matsuri]] held throughout the former [[:en:Sendai Domain|Sendai Domain]] to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=}}, [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]]. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with [[:en:August 7|August 7]], the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of [[:en:July 7|July 7]] in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other [[:en:Arcade (architecture)|arcade]] streets around [[:en:Sendai Station (Miyagi)|Sendai Station]]. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by [[:en:Date Masamune|Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the [[:en:Great Tenmei famine|Tenmei Famine]], a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the [[:en:Solar calendar|Solar calendar]], further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to [[:en:August 6|August 6]]–[[:en:August 8|8]], aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the [[:en:Bombing of Sendai in World War II|Sendai Air Raid]]. It was fully restored in 1947 during the [[:en:Hirohito|Shōwa Emperor]]’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during [[:en:Japanese economic miracle|Japan's postwar economic growth]], evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * [[:en:Orizuru|Orizuru]]: Longevity. * [[:en:Kinchaku|Kinchaku]]: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * [[:en:Cast net|Tōami]]: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=}}: Threads woven by [[:en:Zhinü|Orihime]]. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=}}, often paired with [[:en:Kusudama|kusudama]]. stop (August 4, 2007)]] [[File:Sendai tanabata matsuri 2008-8-8.webm|right|thumb|220px|Sendai Tanabata Matsuri (August 8, 2008)]] [[File:Vegalta SENDAI Tanabata, the decorations of Sendai Star Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting [[:en:Vegalta Sendai|Vegalta Sendai]] (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and [[:en:Festival|Matsuri]] held throughout the former [[:en:Sendai Domain|Sendai Domain]] to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 節句}}, [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]]. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with [[:en:August 7|August 7]], the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of [[:en:July 7|July 7]] in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other [[:en:Arcade (architecture)|arcade]] streets around [[:en:Sendai Station (Miyagi)|Sendai Station]]. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by [[:en:Date Masamune|Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the [[:en:Great Tenmei famine|Tenmei Famine]], a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the [[:en:Solar calendar|Solar calendar]], further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to [[:en:August 6|August 6]]–[[:en:August 8|8]], aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the [[:en:Bombing of Sendai in World War II|Sendai Air Raid]]. It was fully restored in 1947 during the [[:en:Hirohito|Shōwa Emperor]]’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during [[:en:Japanese economic miracle|Japan's postwar economic growth]], evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * [[:en:Orizuru|Orizuru]]: Longevity. * [[:en:Kinchaku|Kinchaku]]: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * [[:en:Cast net|Tōami]]: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ごみ箱}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}: Threads woven by [[:en:Zhinü|Orihime]]. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}, often paired with [[:en:Kusudama|kusudama]]. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|qq=}} * {{ill|Zuihōden Tanabata supporting [[:en:Vegalta Sendai|Vegalta Sendai]] (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and [[:en:Festival|Matsuri]] held throughout the former [[:en:Sendai Domain|Sendai Domain]] to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 節句}}, [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]]. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with [[:en:August 7|August 7]], the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of [[:en:July 7|July 7]] in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other [[:en:Arcade (architecture)|arcade]] streets around [[:en:Sendai Station (Miyagi)|Sendai Station]]. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by [[:en:Date Masamune|Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the [[:en:Great Tenmei famine|Tenmei Famine]], a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the [[:en:Solar calendar|Solar calendar]], further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to [[:en:August 6|August 6]]–[[:en:August 8|8]], aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the [[:en:Bombing of Sendai in World War II|Sendai Air Raid]]. It was fully restored in 1947 during the [[:en:Hirohito|Shōwa Emperor]]’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during [[:en:Japanese economic miracle|Japan's postwar economic growth]], evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * [[:en:Orizuru|Orizuru]]: Longevity. * [[:en:Kinchaku|Kinchaku]]: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * [[:en:Cast net|Tōami]]: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ごみ箱}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}: Threads woven by [[:en:Zhinü|Orihime]]. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}, often paired with [[:en:Kusudama|kusudama]]. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting [[:en:Vegalta Sendai|Vegalta Sendai]] (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and [[:en:Festival|Matsuri]] held throughout the former [[:en:Sendai Domain|Sendai Domain]] to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 節句}}, [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]]. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with [[:en:August 7|August 7]], the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of [[:en:July 7|July 7]] in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other [[:en:Arcade (architecture)|arcade]] streets around [[:en:Sendai Station (Miyagi)|Sendai Station]]. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by [[:en:Date Masamune|Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the [[:en:Great Tenmei famine|Tenmei Famine]], a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the [[:en:Solar calendar|Solar calendar]], further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to [[:en:August 6|August 6]]–[[:en:August 8|8]], aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the [[:en:Bombing of Sendai in World War II|Sendai Air Raid]]. It was fully restored in 1947 during the [[:en:Hirohito|Shōwa Emperor]]’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during [[:en:Japanese economic miracle|Japan's postwar economic growth]], evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * [[:en:Orizuru|Orizuru]]: Longevity. * [[:en:Kinchaku|Kinchaku]]: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * [[:en:Cast net|Tōami]]: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ごみ箱}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}: Threads woven by [[:en:Zhinü|Orihime]]. stop (August 4, 2007)]] [[File:Sendai tanabata matsuri 2008-8-8.webm|right|thumb|220px|Sendai Tanabata Matsuri (August 8, 2008)]] [[File:Vegalta SENDAI Tanabata, the decorations of Sendai Star Festival.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Decorations supporting [[:en:Vegalta Sendai|Vegalta Sendai]] (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and [[:en:Festival|Matsuri]] held throughout the former [[:en:Sendai Domain|Sendai Domain]] to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 節句}}, [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]]. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Tohoku Three Great Festivals|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with [[:en:August 7|August 7]], the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of [[:en:July 7|July 7]] in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other [[:en:Arcade (architecture)|arcade]] streets around [[:en:Sendai Station (Miyagi)|Sendai Station]]. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by [[:en:Date Masamune|Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the [[:en:Great Tenmei famine|Tenmei Famine]], a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the [[:en:Solar calendar|Solar calendar]], further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to [[:en:August 6|August 6]]–[[:en:August 8|8]], aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the [[:en:Bombing of Sendai in World War II|Sendai Air Raid]]. It was fully restored in 1947 during the [[:en:Hirohito|Shōwa Emperor]]’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during [[:en:Japanese economic miracle|Japan's postwar economic growth]], evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * [[:en:Orizuru|Orizuru]]: Longevity. * [[:en:Kinchaku|Kinchaku]]: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * [[:en:Cast net|Tōami]]: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ごみ箱}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}: Threads woven by [[:en:Zhinü|Orihime]]. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}, often paired with [[:en:Kusudama|kusudama]]. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|ja|仙台七夕花火祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendai Tanabata Fireworks Festival|qq=}} * {{ill|Zuihōden Tanabata The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tohoku|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tohoku|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with [[:en:August 7|August 7]], the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of [[:en:July 7|July 7]] in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other [[:en:Arcade (architecture)|arcade]] streets around [[:en:Sendai Station (Miyagi)|Sendai Station]]. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by [[:en:Date Masamune|Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the [[:en:Great Tenmei famine|Tenmei Famine]], a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the [[:en:Solar calendar|Solar calendar]], further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to [[:en:August 6|August 6]]–[[:en:August 8|8]], aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the [[:en:Bombing of Sendai in World War II|Sendai Air Raid]]. It was fully restored in 1947 during the [[:en:Hirohito|Shōwa Emperor]]’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during [[:en:Japanese economic miracle|Japan's postwar economic growth]], evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * [[:en:Orizuru|Orizuru]]: Longevity. * [[:en:Kinchaku|Kinchaku]]: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * [[:en:Cast net|Tōami]]: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ごみ箱}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}: Threads woven by [[:en:Zhinü|Orihime]]. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}, often paired with [[:en:Kusudama|kusudama]]. supporting [[:en:Vegalta Sendai|Vegalta Sendai]] (August 6, 2009)]] '''Sendai Tanabata''' (仙台七夕) is an annual {{ill|seasonal event|ja|年中行事|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/seasonal event|qq=}} and [[:en:Festival|Matsuri]] held throughout the former [[:en:Sendai Domain|Sendai Domain]] to celebrate one of the {{ill|Gosekku|ja|五節句|Gosekku=Gosekku|lt=five seasonal festivals|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosekku|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 節句}}, [[:en:Qixi Festival|Tanabata]]. Locally, it is also known as "Tanabata-san." The '''Sendai Tanabata Matsuri''', held in [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]], is particularly famous and is counted among the {{ill|Three Great Festivals of Tohoku|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tohoku|lt=Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|ja|東北三大祭り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Great Festivals of Tōhoku|qq=}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20220730-JKJJ3QED5NMSJJB2HNJRLFKAYY/|title=東北三大祭り　観客分散、観覧席削減…感染対策に腐心|publisher=産経ニュース|date=2022-07-30|accessdate=2022-07-30}} == Overview == The Sendai Tanabata Matsuri is held annually for three days, with [[:en:August 7|August 7]], the {{ill|calendar|ja|月遅れ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/calendar|qq=}} equivalent of [[:en:July 7|July 7]] in the lunar calendar, as its centerpiece. Large-scale decorations are displayed in {{ill|Ichibanchō|ja|一番町 (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichibanchō|qq=}}, {{ill|Chūō-dōri|ja|中央通り (仙台市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūō-dōri|qq=}}, and other [[:en:Arcade (architecture)|arcade]] streets around [[:en:Sendai Station (Miyagi)|Sendai Station]]. Decorations are also spread across local shopping districts, businesses, and homes throughout the city, with approximately 3,000 decorations.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sendaitanabata.com/event/index.html |title=周辺部七夕バスツアー |publisher=仙台七夕まつり |accessdate=2024-05-26 }} The festival attracts over 2 million visitors annually. The event also influences other regions, with decorative techniques developed in Sendai being adopted in metropolitan areas, such as the Tokyo metropolitan region. Companies and stations across Japan utilize Tanabata decorations created by specialized artisans, further spreading Sendai’s tradition. == History == The origins of the Sendai Tanabata Matsuri are traced back to the early Edo Period when it was promoted by [[:en:Date Masamune|Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai Domain, to encourage cultural refinement among women. By the mid-Edo Period, the Tanabata tradition had become widespread across Japan. In 1783, during the [[:en:Great Tenmei famine|Tenmei Famine]], a grand celebration was held in Sendai to restore public morale. The Tanabata tradition began to decline after 1873 with the adoption of the [[:en:Solar calendar|Solar calendar]], further exacerbated by economic difficulties following World War I. In 1927, concerned merchants revived the custom with large-scale decorations, which attracted large crowds. From 1928, the festival was shifted to [[:en:August 6|August 6]]–[[:en:August 8|8]], aligning with the lunar calendar’s "month delay," and featured a decoration contest in connection with the {{ill|Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|ja|東北産業博覧会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōhoku Industrial Exhibition|qq=}}. The festival was revived after World War II with 52 bamboo decorations in 1946 amidst the ruins caused by the [[:en:Bombing of Sendai in World War II|Sendai Air Raid]]. It was fully restored in 1947 during the [[:en:Hirohito|Shōwa Emperor]]’s visit, with 5,000 bamboo decorations lining the streets. The festival gained nationwide attention during [[:en:Japanese economic miracle|Japan's postwar economic growth]], evolving into a major tourist attraction and one of Tōhoku's three great festivals. == Tanabata Decorations == The festival's "Seven Decorations" each symbolize a unique wish: * {{ill|Tanzaku|ja|短冊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tanzaku|qq=}}: For academic and literary improvement. * {{ill|Kamigoromo|ja|紙衣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigoromo|qq=}}: Protection from illness and disaster. * [[:en:Orizuru|Orizuru]]: Longevity. * [[:en:Kinchaku|Kinchaku]]: Wealth, prosperity, and thrift. * [[:en:Cast net|Tōami]]: Abundant fishing hauls. * {{ill|Kuzukago|ja|くずかご|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuzukago|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ごみ箱}}: Cleanliness and thrift. * {{ill|Fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}: Threads woven by [[:en:Zhinü|Orihime]]. The prominent decoration is the {{ill|fukinagashi|ja|吹き流し|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/fukinagashi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 吹流し}}, often paired with [[:en:Kusudama|kusudama]]. Unique features of the festival include the exclusive use of paper-based decorations, avoiding plastics or vinyl. == Related Events == * {{ill|Sendai Tanabata Fireworks
